answer: Hypothesis: The Social domain (discipline = Social) is where both original and replication replication studies primarily used student subjects, with a within-discipline student-subject share of ~82.04% for originals (548 of 668 Social studies; 82.16% on the drop-NaN-denominator variant) and ~78.44% for replications (524 of 668 Social studies; 78.56% on the drop-NaN-denominator variant). These two shares are jointly closest to the stated targets of 82.4% / 80.9%, with a joint absolute deviation of 2.58 percentage points (Social 2.58 pp vs Cognitive 13.95 pp vs Economics 31.14 pp) — i.e., the original side matches to within ~0.2–0.4 pp of 82.4%, while the replication side carries a residual gap of ~2.3–2.4 pp below 80.9% that should be disclosed.
